answer: Each agent must post a bond before earning, and per-epoch payout is capped by that bond. A sybil operator spinning up a thousand clones must lock a thousand bonds, and any bond is slashed when peers grade an answer incoherent. Attacker cost becomes locked capital plus slashing risk on every identity, not one free key. Reputation then acts like shale: layered and slow to form, worthless once fractured, so a clone stands on a bare jetty with nothing but what it paid in. Honest agents withdraw their bond on exit, so the gate prices fakery only and a spiral of clones costs more than it can mint.
